extracted.intended_audience: Congressional appropriations staff, USPTO management, and trademark stakeholders (applicants, practitioners, and program managers)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and program objectives governing USPTO trademark examination, quality assurance, publication/opposition and maintenance procedures, plus cross-cutting IT, training, and administrative performance goals used to evaluate and run the Trademark Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to registration under the Trademark Act
rubrics_metrics.description: An examining attorney determines whether the mark in each newly filed application is entitled to registration under the provisions of the Trademark Act of 1946, as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examining attorneys evaluate many types of marks—trademarks, service marks, certification marks, and collective membership marks—against the criteria for registrability set out in the Trademark Act; based upon their evaluation, examining attorneys decide to approve or deny an application for registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and evaluation for confusing similarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The examining attorney searches previously filed and registered marks to evaluate whether a conflict exists and to determine whether the mark in the subject application is confusingly similar to an existing mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examining attorneys search a database of more than 3 million registered marks and 1.2 million pending marks; the process uses electronically tagged application data, international classification, and design search codes to facilitate searching and examination; the result of the search informs approval or refusal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication prior to registration and opposition process
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved applications are published prior to registration to notify interested parties who may file an opposition to the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademarks publishes approved applications to allow oppositions; marks are registered if unopposed or if they survive any filed opposition; publication therefore functions as notice and an opportunity for third parties to challenge registrability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent-to-use applications and Statement of Use/Notice of Allowance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Marks filed based on intent to use receive a notice of allowance following the opposition period if unopposed or if they survive any filed opposition, and registration occurs after the applicant files a Statement of Use and the USPTO accepts it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural sequence (intent-to-use → notice of allowance → Statement of Use → registration) is required to convert an ITU application into a registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance review of first and final office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the quality assurance program, Trademarks reviews the results of an examining attorney’s first and final office actions for quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews assess the quality of the substantive basis of decisions, search strategy, evidence, and writing. Data collected from these reviews inform targeted electronic and traditional training initiatives addressing specific areas for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional Office Action standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An Exceptional Office Action emphasizes comprehensive excellence in final office actions and expands upon existing standards for correct decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Exceptional Office Action reflects correct decision-making, includes excellent evidentiary support, and is exceptionally well written; the initiative aims to 'raise the bar' for final actions beyond baseline first/final action standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examining attorney competency and training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO ensures examining attorneys possess the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform their jobs and improve examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademarks provides self-paced e-learning tutorials and implements new e-learning modules throughout the year based on topics identified through quality review evaluations; training is targeted based on QA data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination for completeness and statutory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks examines filings for completeness and compliance with statutory requirements to ensure the accuracy of registered marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input processing encompasses processing of international applications (Madrid Protocol) and automated transfer of tagged application data to appropriate fields; completeness and statutory compliance are prerequisites to processing and registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance, renewal, and incontestability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners can maintain registrations indefinitely if the registered mark is in use; specific affidavits and renewal filings are required at statutory intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Between the fifth and sixth years after registration, the owner must file an affidavit attesting to use; to renew, an acceptable affidavit of use and an application for renewal must be filed within one year before the end of each 10-year registration period. Owners on the Principal Register may claim incontestability after five consecutive years of continuous use post-registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random audit of maintenance and renewal filings
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO conducts random audits of marks submitted for maintenance or renewal to verify that goods and services continue to be used in commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the required affidavit and proof of use, or to substantiate use when audited, results in cancellation of the registration. Audits serve to remove marks no longer in use and to preserve clearance opportunities for new applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Trials and Appeals (TTAB) review and opposition/cancellation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Trademark Judges (ATJs) on the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB) review adverse registrability determinations and preside over opposition and cancellation proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTAB proceedings adjudicate disputes where an interested party challenges registration on grounds of likely harm; ATJs review examining attorneys’ refusals when applicants appeal adverse determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Information Resources objective: reduce examination processing time
rubrics_metrics.description: One key objective is to reduce examination processing time by modernizing the TM Exam platform and associated components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include replacing outdated legacy software with modern, common services and migrating systems to the cloud to streamline processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Information Resources objective: improve internal user experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve internal user experience by resolving defects and infrastructural issues that cause functionality problems and outages and by modernizing legacy systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolving inefficient workflows and improving system reliability are measures of success for internal user experience improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Information Resources objective: improve application submission and examination quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Streamline the application submission process and improve examination quality through modern systems and better tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts to simplify submission workflows and provide better examination tooling are intended to improve both customer submissions and examiner performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Cutting Functions program objectives (organizational goals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cross-Cutting Functions Program aims to promote organizational excellence, quality customer experiences (CXs), sound resource management, reliable workforce planning, and modernized IT systems and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major objectives include: bringing education and awareness to IP's role in prosperity/security; promoting respect for IP; combating IP theft; advancing a performance-based culture and employee engagement; managing user fees effectively; modernizing secure and scalable technology; and making data-driven decisions and leveraging automation. Costs are allocated to Patent and Trademark Programs using ABI analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Technology Infrastructure objectives: security, resiliency, emerging technology
rubrics_metrics.description: IT Infrastructure and IT Support Services prioritize Security, Resiliency, and Emerging Technology as key objectives to support USPTO operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security protects systems and data against digital attacks; resiliency ensures continuous operations and high availability; emerging technology efforts (cloud, AI, etc.) explore and deliver new capabilities to support timely decision-making and mission continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy, international engagement, and operational support responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: OPIA establishes trademark examination policy standards, serves as authority on trademark laws/rules/examining practices, implements treaty obligations and judicial/TTAB decisions, and maintains the Trademark Manual of Examining Procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPIA participates in multilateral organizations (e.g., WIPO, WTO), supports IP work-sharing initiatives (IP5), and provides technical expertise in international IP policy; policy development and international coordination are program performance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outreach, training, and international capacity-building (GIPA and IP Attaché programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: GIPA and the IP Attaché Program provide training, technical assistance, and outreach to improve IP protection and enforcement internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GIPA offers web-based and on-site training, 'train the trainers' programs, and region-specific programming; the IP Attaché Program places technical experts abroad to influence laws, regulations, and IPR practices and to support U.S. stakeholders—program reach/coverage and capacity are performance metrics.
